title: Support for Industry and Consumers Given Higher Electricity Prices and Recent Exit of Electricity Retailers
what_it_is: Support for Industry and Consumers Given Higher Electricity Prices and Recent Exit of Electricity Retailers

sections.label: Energy crunch and electricity retailers
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister about the impact of the China and India energy crunch on Singapore electricity prices, EMA strategies, assistance for low-income families, and retailer viability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the impact of the energy supply crunch in China and India on electricity prices in Singapore; (b) what are the Energy Market Authority’s strategies to cushion the impact of the international energy supply crunch on the stability of energy supply and electricity prices in Singapore; and (c) whether additional assistance will be given to low-income families to cope with the rise in electricity prices from 1 October 2021, if such rates increase were to continue beyond 31 December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry following the recent collapse of several electricity retailers (a) what is the Ministry’s assessment of the business viability of the remaining electricity retailers; and (b) what steps will the Ministry take to maintain a competitive electricity market in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry given the recent pull out of iSwitch Energy from the open electricity market (a) what is the Ministry’s current risk assessment of more retailers exiting the market due to the increases in the price of gas; (b) whether the current recourse options for consumers are sufficient and satisfactory should more retailers exit; (c) whether the Ministry is considering a longer notice period for retailers when they choose to exit the market so that consumers are better safeguarded; and (d) what are the critical success factors to ensure the continued success of Singapore’s open energy market.

sections.label: Electricity retailer exits and consumers
sections.summary: Questions ask whether retailer exits show overly aggressive pricing, whether a review of retailer numbers is planned, and whether SP Group will honour contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether the recent exits of iSwitch Energy, SilverCloud Energy and Ohm Energy due to the volatile global electricity market are a sign that the Open Energy Market (OEM) retailers have been too aggressive in their pricing to attract customers; (b) whether the Ministry will be doing a review to determine the optimal number of retailers in the Open Energy Market; and (c) whether there are plans to include more measures to better protect consumers from sudden exits by the OEM retailers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether the SP Group will continue to honour the prices and terms of existing contracts between the private electricity retailers who recently quit the Open Energy Market and their affected users until the contracts’ expiration; and (b) how will this series of exits affect the intended liberalisation of the energy market in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the root cause of energy retailers’ exit from the market; (b) what is the impact to businesses and households; and (c) what are the additional measures taken to ensure a stable energy market.

sections.label: Retailer exits and piped natural gas
sections.summary: Questions ask how many households return to SP Group, expected price increases, assistance, and reasons for the West Natuna piped natural gas curtailment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry regarding the recent exit of several electricity retailers from the open electricity market (a) how many households are expected to have their contracts transferred back to SP Group in the next few months; (b) what is the expected increase in electricity prices they will face with this change; and (c) how is the Ministry assisting households negatively affected by these changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what are the reasons for the recent curtailment of piped natural gas (PNG) from West Natuna; (b) what other disruptions to PNG supplies have been experienced in the past six months; (c) whether Singapore has had to use its reserves of liquified natural gas; (d) how long will these reserves last under current conditions; and (e) how is the Ministry exploring alternatives to natural gas for power generation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As a result, spot gas prices have risen by around five times, since March 2021.

sections.label: West Natuna gas supply incident
sections.summary: An incident at the upstream gas production facility in July affected West Natuna's gas supply to Singapore, causing a fall in overall gas supply of about 3% since September 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: By and large, the supply of PNG has been relatively stable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: However, due to an incident at the upstream gas production facility in July this year, West Natuna’s gas supply to Singapore has been affected resulting in a fall in overall gas supply by about 3% since September 2021.

sections.label: Gas options and fuel reserves
sections.summary: Gas users have more options to procure gas, and gencos are required to stockpile at least 60 days of fuel reserves for supply disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Gas users in Singapore now have more options to procure the gas they require.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We also require power generation companies, or gencos, to stockpile at least 60 days of fuel reserves, in the event of disruptions to our natural gas supply.

sections.label: EMA review of measures
sections.summary: EMA will review if these measures are still needed by 31 March 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: EMA will review if these measures are still needed by 31 March 2022.

sections.label: Five electricity retailers leaving market
sections.summary: Five electricity retailers announced plans to leave the market, supplying about 9% of all electricity consumers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Over the last three weeks, five electricity retailers – iSwitch, Ohm Energy, Best Electricity, UGS, SilverCloud Energy – have announced their plans to leave the market.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: These five retailers supply to about 9% of all electricity consumers.

sections.label: Households and businesses transferred
sections.summary: As of end October 2021, about 140,000 households and 11,000 business accounts will be transferred to another retailer or back to SP Group.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As of end October 2021, about 140,000 households and 11,000 business accounts will either be transferred to another retailer, or back to SP Group.

sections.label: Households switched to retailers
sections.summary: About half of all households, or about 746,000 household accounts, have switched to buying electricity from electricity retailers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To date, about half of all households, or about 746,000 households accounts, have switched to buying electricity from electricity retailers.

sections.label: Retailer requirements and insufficient measures
sections.summary: Retailers must show management experience, hedge at least 50% of wholesale price risk and submit financial statements to EMA, but measures were insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For example, retailers have to demonstrate that their management team possesses the relevant experience in energy retailing or trading, they have to consistently hedge at least 50% of their wholesale electricity price risk and they have to submit financial statements to EMA, which allows EMA to monitor their financial health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In hindsight, these are necessary but for a severe stress test such as this, the measures were insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Some retailers were ill-prepared to weather the storm.

sections.label: Consumers on price plans
sections.summary: Ninety-nine percent of household consumers are on standard price plans or the regulated tariff, and about 96% of businesses are on fixed price or discount-off-tariff plans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Ninety-nine percent of household consumers are on standard price plans with retailers or the regulated tariff rate and about 96% of businesses are on fixed price or discount-off-tariff plans.

sections.label: Targeted assistance and U-Save rebates
sections.summary: The Government will provide focused and targeted assistance to eligible consumer groups, and eligible households will continue to receive U-Save rebates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Government will provide focused and targeted assistance to eligible groups of consumers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Eligible households will continue to receive U-Save rebates to support them with their utility expenses.

sections.label: Electricity price increase next year
sections.summary: Most consumers will not see an immediate electricity price increase, but may see one next year as global energy prices rise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: While most consumers will not see an immediate increase in electricity prices, they may see an increase next year with increasing energy prices globally.

sections.label: Sufficient electricity supply secured
sections.summary: An EMA 19 October press release announced that Singapore has sufficient supply.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: What is important is that as we look at securing our supply – I think it was announced in the 19 October press release by EMA – in terms of the supply, we have sufficient supply.

sections.label: Fuel stockpiles and generation capacity
sections.summary: Generation companies must hold fuel stockpiles lasting at least 60 days, standby fuel facilities were secured in mid-October, and generation capacity is sufficient.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: All generation companies will need to comply with our requirements to have a fuel stockpiles that will last at least 60 days of operation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The standby fuel facilities are necessary to ensure we have sufficient fuel in Singapore to meet our electricity demand.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Hence, we took the pre-emptive step in mid-October to secure this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: EMA will continue to review the need to maintain this facility once the global energy situation stabilises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, to reassure Ms Jessica Tan and Members of the House, our generation capacity is sufficient.

sections.label: Prudential safeguards for consumers
sections.summary: Before the energy crunch, prudential requirements were largely adequate, with safeguards such as household deposit protection and 50% minimum hedging requirements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Prior to the current energy crunch, our prudential requirements were largely adequate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We put in place safeguards to protect consumer interests, such as safeguarding the deposits of households and also the minimum hedging requirements of 50%.

sections.label: Enhanced licensing for OEM retailers
sections.summary: EMA will enhance licencing requirements for OEM retailers and strengthen consumer protection moving forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: EMA will enhance the licencing requirements for the OEM retailers and strengthen protection even more for consumers moving forward.

sections.label: Novation under retail code
sections.summary: Under the Code of Conduct for retail electricity licensees, retailers must approach other retailers to attempt to novate customers on the same contractual terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Related question under the Code of Conduct for retail electricity licensees, retailers are required to approach other retailers to attempt to novate their customers on the same contractual terms.

sections.label: Energy Bill and EMA powers
sections.summary: A Bill on energy resilience measures will be put up, and EMA has received no complaints about OEM retailers pre-terminating contracts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Tomorrow, I would be also putting up a Bill, the Energy (Resilience Measures and Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And if so, what powers does EMA have to ensure consumers are fairly treated?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Thus far, EMA has not received any complaints from consumers about the OEM retailers pre-terminating their contracts.

sections.label: U-Save rebates for lower-income households
sections.summary: Vouchers for U-Save rebates help lower-income households with their utility bills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the lower-income households, we have the vouchers for the U-Save rebates which effectively help them in terms of the utility bills.

sections.label: Exploring further help with MOF
sections.summary: Despite existing rebates, further means to help are being explored with MOF.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the rebates that are already in existence, we are also exploring with MOF further means to help.

sections.label: Global gas supply contractual obligations
sections.summary: Contractual obligations and compensation benchmarks apply if suppliers cannot supply the agreed amount of gas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In terms of the global gas situation, the Member asked about what kind of leverage we have.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: There are contractual obligations, if they are not able to supply the agreed amount of gas, there are compensation benchmarks.

sections.label: Regulated tariffs reflect generation cost
sections.summary: Regulated tariffs reflect the long-run marginal cost of generating electricity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The regulated tariffs reflect the long-run marginal cost of generating electricity.

sections.label: Mitigating growth of imported electricity
sections.summary: Efforts focus on mitigating the growth gradient, as over 95% of electricity comes from imported natural gas and solar could meet only about 4% to 6% of needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: What we can try to do, very, very hard, is to try to mitigate and manage the gradient of that growth.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We import all of our electricity, 95% of our electricity, more than that is through natural gas, which is imported.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Even if I were to cover all the rooftops of the HDB flats, the JTC buildings with solar panels – we use vertical solar panels today and we cover our floating reservoirs, all the vast expanse of space – we probably can generate maybe at peak, well not at peak, but probably between 4% and 5% or 6% of our needs.

sections.label: Support for low-income households
sections.summary: The Government will keep supporting low-income households through vouchers and rebates as the gap between market and regulated electricity tariffs narrows.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Government will continue to support the low-income households through all these vouchers and rebates and so on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But I think whether we like it or not, as the demand and supply situation continues to tighten, the gap between the open electricity market and the regulated tariffs will continue to narrow.
